vocabulary.definition: Warm-blooded, egg-laying animals, most of which are able to fly. Their features include feathers, powerful wings, and hollow bones.
An animal that hunts, kills, and eats other animals.
When a bird cleans and smooths its feathers with its beak.
The rigid framework (usually of bone or cartilage) of an animal’s body.
Sweet liquid produced by flowers; some birds and insects feed on it.
Birds of prey that feed wholly or chiefly on meat taken by hunting or on carrion.
To fly or dive down swiftly, usually to catch prey.
Moving from one place to another according to the seasons, usually to find food or breed.
A cold-blooded, usually egg-laying vertebrate covered with scales or horny plates that breathes through lungs.
An animal that has a backbone.
An animal whose body temperature depends on their surroundings.
Cold-blooded animals that live in water. Most have gills that absorb oxygen from the water and the majority have fins and scales.
Feathery structures on the side of a fish’s head that extract oxygen from the water.
A localized population of a species or organism.
The transfer of pollen from anther to stigma.
A class of arthropods including spiders, scorpions, mites, and ticks, having a segmented body divided into two regions.
A bony case or shield covering the back or part of the back of an animal.
To feed on the carcasses of other animals.
An animal that helps to decay and recycle vast amounts of organic waste.
A long, bendy, armlike body part that aquatic animals such as squid and cuttlefish use for touching and grasping.

locations.name: Florida
locations.significance: Its swamps, rivers, and lakes serve as the primary habitat for the American alligator.

locations.name: Columbia
locations.significance: Home to the endangered Doris Swanson’s poison dart frog, whose territory covers less than 0.2 square miles of forest here.

locations.name: Indian Ocean
locations.significance: The warm shallow waters around coral reefs here are the habitat for the giant grouper fish.

locations.name: Pacific Ocean
locations.significance: The western and central parts of this ocean provide a habitat for the giant grouper fish.

locations.name: Caribbean
locations.significance: The waters where the endangered staghorn coral forms branching shapes like antlers on upper to mid-reef slopes.

locations.name: Europe
locations.significance: One of the regions where the Golden Eagle is found soaring through the sky.

locations.name: Asia
locations.significance: A continent where the Golden Eagle is commonly found.

locations.name: North Africa
locations.significance: A geographic region that supports populations of the Golden Eagle.

trueFalse.statement: Hard corals build huge coral reefs using an external skeleton made of limestone.
trueFalse.correction: Hard corals have an internal skeleton made of limestone, not an external one.

trueFalse.statement: Soft corals often look like plants and possess a flexible internal skeleton.
trueFalse.correction: They have a flexible internal skeleton that allows them to sway in the water.

trueFalse.statement: All corals grow from one tiny animal called a polyp when it produces new polyps to create a coral.
trueFalse.correction: Polyps are the building blocks of coral reefs.

trueFalse.statement: The orange cup coral attaches to rocks along the deep ocean floor.
trueFalse.correction: The orange cup coral actually attaches to rocks in tidal pools.

trueFalse.statement: The staghorn coral is located in upper to mid-reef slopes and lagoons in waters of the Caribbean.
trueFalse.correction: It thrives in the shallow waters of the Caribbean.

trueFalse.statement: The polyps that form a brain coral arrange themselves in wandering lines giving it a wrinkled appearance like a brain.
trueFalse.correction: This unique arrangement gives the brain coral its name.

trueFalse.statement: Mute swans make their nests high in trees away from predators.
trueFalse.correction: It is the Mandarin duck that makes its nest high in trees, not the mute swan.

trueFalse.statement: The American alligator spends almost all of its time in fresh water and is a good swimmer that primarily hunts fish.
trueFalse.correction: That describes the Gharial; the American alligator lives in swamps, rivers, and lakes of Florida.

trueFalse.statement: The golden poison dart frog is the most poisonous frog on earth, containing enough poison in its skin to kill 10 humans.
trueFalse.correction: It is considered one of the most toxic animals on the planet.

trueFalse.statement: Bony fish account for 9 out of 10 species of fish.
trueFalse.correction: Bony fish are the most diverse and abundant class of fish.

trueFalse.statement: The estuarine stonefish has 13 venomous spines along its back that could kill a human if stepped on.
trueFalse.correction: It is the most venomous fish in the world.

trueFalse.statement: Giant grouper fish live in large schools in the deep ocean.
trueFalse.correction: They live alone in warm, shallow waters around coral reefs.

trueFalse.statement: Jellyfish move using jet propulsion when they aren't floating in the current.
trueFalse.correction: They contract their bell to push water out and propel themselves forward.

trueFalse.statement: A treehopper avoids predators by disguising itself as a thorn on a branch.
trueFalse.correction: This disguise, along with foul-tasting chemicals, protects them from being eaten.

trueFalse.statement: The blue starfish cannot survive if its limbs are torn apart.
trueFalse.correction: The blue starfish can regrow into 5 separate starfish even if all 5 limbs are torn apart.

quiz.question: What is the term for when a bird cleans and smooths its feathers with its beak?
Which characteristic is NOT typical of a bird?
Where does the extremely vulnerable Doris Swanson’s poison dart frog live?
How many venomous spines does the estuarine stonefish have along its back?
Which crocodile feeds by pulling its large prey into the water and spinning around to tear off chunks?
Which frog collects poison from the bugs it eats and deposits the poison on its skin?
options: Green and black poison dart frog

quiz.question: What do manta rays use to funnel water and prey into their mouths?
options: Large lobes on the side of the head
quiz.correctAnswer: Large lobes on the side of the head

quiz.question: Which deep-sea fish has a mouth much wider than its body and an expanding stomach to consume food larger than itself?
Which poor swimmer dwells at 3,280 ft deep and lies in wait for its prey?
Which endangered coral forms branching shapes like antlers in the waters of the Caribbean?
What insect avoids predators by disguising itself as a thorn and containing foul-tasting chemicals?
Which sea creature can regrow into separate individuals if its limbs are completely torn apart?
What is the favorite food of the Crown-of-thorns starfish, which can eat voraciously and damage habitats?
How does the common starfish eat bivalve mollusks like mussels and clams?
options: Pushing its stomach out of its body and inside the shell
Crushing the shell with its powerful jaws
Injecting venom to dissolve the shell from the outside
quiz.correctAnswer: Pushing its stomach out of its body and inside the shell

quiz.question: What material makes up the internal skeleton of hard corals?
